9	------------------------------------------------------------------------
10	
11	**Pipenv** is a Python virtualenv management tool that supports a multitude of systems and nicely bridges the gaps between pip, python (using system python, pyenv or asdf) and virtualenv.
12	*Linux, macOS, and Windows are all first-class citizens in pipenv.*
13	
14	Pipenv automatically creates and manages a virtualenv for your projects, as well as adds/removes packages from your `Pipfile` as you install/uninstall packages. It also generates a project `Pipfile.lock`, which is used to produce deterministic builds.
15	
16	Pipenv is primarily meant to provide users and developers of applications with an easy method to arrive at a consistent working project environment.
17	
18	The problems that Pipenv seeks to solve are multi-faceted:
19	
20	- You no longer need to use `pip` and `virtualenv` separately: they work together.
21	- Managing a `requirements.txt` file with package hashes can be problematic.  Pipenv uses `Pipfile` and `Pipfile.lock` to separate abstract dependency declarations from the last tested combination.
22	- Hashes are documented in the lock file which are verified during install. Security considerations are put first.
23	- Strongly encourage the use of the latest versions of dependencies to minimize security risks [arising from outdated components](https://www.owasp.org/index.php/Top_10-2017_A9-Using_Components_with_Known_Vulnerabilities).
24	- Gives you insight into your dependency graph (e.g. `$ pipenv graph`).
25	- Streamline development workflow by supporting local customizations with `.env` files.
